span: an illegality with regard to a mere erroneous application of law would not be a ground for interference
why: Headnote holding that mere erroneous application of law is not a ground under s.34.

span: Mere possibility of an alternative view on facts or interpretation of the contract does not entitle courts to reverse the findings of the arbitral tribunal
why: Headnote holding: a possible alternative interpretation of the contract is not a ground to interfere.

span: either to set aside an award or remand the matter under the circumstances mentioned in Section 34
why: Headnote about whether a court can modify an award; it confirms the limited remedy but does not decide whether an erroneous interpretation of a contract is a ground.

span: The Arbitrator erred in awarding pendente lite and future interest on the amount due and payable to the contractor under the contract in question
why: Court sets aside the award of interest because the arbitrator acted contrary to the contract's clause 16(2) barring interest — an award corrected for a wrong application of the contract.

span: The purpose of Section 34 is to strike a balance between Court’s appellate powers and integrity of the arbitral process.
why: General framing of s.34's limited grounds before analysing the award.

span: However, an illegality with regard to a mere erroneous application of law would not be a ground for interference.
why: Court states it is settled that a court under s.34 does not reappreciate and that mere erroneous application of law is not a ground for interference.
